nodes.summary: If a skip list is valid, then the keys of the pairs in its bottom-level abstraction, read in order, form a list without duplicates.
nodes.title: Keys of a valid skip list are distinct

nodes.summary: The bottom-level abstraction of a skip list is the association list obtained from its bottom-level nodes, in order, by keeping the key-value pair $(k, v)$ of each node and forgetting its tower height.
nodes.title: Bottom-level abstraction of a skip list

nodes.summary: For every search key, every level $i$ and every list $L$ of skip-list nodes, advancing the search at level $i$ on $L$ returns a suffix of $L$.
nodes.title: One search step returns a suffix

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a search key, $i$ a zero-based level and $L$ a list of skip-list nodes. Let $P$ be the longest prefix of $L$ whose nodes all have keys less than $k$. If some node of $P$ has tower height greater than $i$ (so it is visible at level $i$), advancing at level $i$ returns the part of $L$ after the last such node; otherwise it returns $L$ unchanged.
nodes.title: One level of skip-list search

nodes.summary: The empty skip list is the skip list with no nodes.
nodes.title: Empty skip list

nodes.summary: A skip-list node consists of a key, a value and a natural number, the height of its tower. The node itself does not require the height to be positive; positivity is part of the validity invariant of skip lists.
nodes.title: Skip-list node

nodes.summary: Let $e$ be a skip-list entry and $L$ a list of entries, and consider the skip list whose entry list is $e$ followed by $L$. If a key $k$ equals the key of $e$, then erasing $k$ from this skip list leaves the entry list $L$.
nodes.title: Erasing the key of the first entry

nodes.summary: Let $e$ be a skip-list entry and $L$ a list of entries. If the key of $e$ is less than a key $k$, then erasing $k$ from the skip list with entry list $e$ followed by $L$ gives the entry list consisting of $e$ followed by the entry list obtained by erasing $k$ from the skip list with entry list $L$.
nodes.title: Erasing past a smaller first entry

nodes.summary: Let $e$ be a skip-list entry and $L$ a list of entries. If a key $k$ is less than the key of $e$, then erasing $k$ from the skip list with entry list $e$ followed by $L$ leaves the entry list $e$ followed by $L$ unchanged.
nodes.title: Erasing a key below the first entry

nodes.summary: For every key $k$, erasing $k$ from the empty skip list gives the empty skip list.
nodes.title: Erasing from the empty skip list

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a valid skip list and $k$ is a key, then the entry list of the skip list obtained by erasing $k$ from $S$ is the entry list of $S$ with every entry whose key equals $k$ removed, the remaining entries kept in their order.
nodes.title: Erasure on a valid skip list filters out the key

nodes.summary: Given a key $k$ from a linearly ordered type and a skip list $S$, the erasure of $k$ from $S$ is the skip list obtained by scanning the entries of $S$ in order: an entry whose key is less than $k$ is kept and the scan continues; at the first entry whose key is greater than $k$ the scan stops, and that entry and all later ones are kept; at the first entry whose key equals $k$ that entry is removed, the scan stops,…
nodes.title: Skip-list erasure

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a valid skip list and $k$, $k'$ are keys with $k' \ne k$, then the stored tower height of $k'$ in the skip list obtained by erasing $k$ from $S$ is the same as in $S$; in particular $k'$ has no stored height in one exactly when it has none in the other.
nodes.title: Erasure preserves the heights of other keys

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a valid skip list and $k$ is a key, then after erasing $k$ from $S$ the key $k$ has no stored tower height.
nodes.title: The erased key has no stored height

nodes.summary: If a key $k$ does not occur in a skip list $S$, then after inserting $k$ into $S$ with any value and requested height $h$, the stored tower height of $k$ is $\max(1, h)$.
nodes.title: Height of a newly inserted key

nodes.summary: Let $S$ be a valid skip list in which the key $k$ has stored tower height $h_0$. Then after inserting $k$ into $S$ with any value and any requested height, the stored tower height of $k$ is still $h_0$.
nodes.title: Reinsertion preserves tower height

nodes.summary: For a key $k$ and a skip list $S$, the stored tower height of $k$ in $S$ is the tower height of the first bottom-level node of $S$ whose key equals $k$ under the given Boolean equality test on keys; it is undefined when no node has key $k$.
nodes.title: Stored tower height of a key

nodes.summary: To insert key $k$ with value $v$ and requested height $h$ into a skip list, scan its bottom-level nodes in order, keeping every node whose key is less than $k$. At the first node whose key is not less than $k$: if its key equals $k$, its value is replaced by $v$ and its tower height is kept; if its key is greater than $k$, a new node with key $k$, value $v$ and tower height $\max(1, h)$ is placed before it. If…
nodes.title: Skip-list insertion

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a valid skip list, $k$ is a key and $i$ is a natural number, then the level-$i$ list of key-value pairs (levels numbered from $0$) of the skip list obtained by erasing $k$ from $S$ is the level-$i$ list of $S$ with every pair whose key equals $k$ removed, the remaining pairs kept in their order.
nodes.title: Erasure removes the key from every level

nodes.summary: If a skip list is valid, then for every level index $i$ (levels are numbered from $0$ at the bottom), no key occurs twice in the list of key-value pairs visible at level $i$.
nodes.title: Keys on each skip-list level are distinct

nodes.summary: If a skip list is valid, then for every level index $i$ (levels are numbered from $0$ at the bottom), the keys in the list of key-value pairs visible at level $i$ are strictly increasing: every pair has a strictly smaller key than every pair after it.
nodes.title: Skip-list levels are sorted by key

nodes.summary: For every skip list and every level index $i$ (levels are numbered from $0$ at the bottom), the list of key-value pairs visible at level $i + 1$ is a subsequence, not necessarily contiguous, of the list of key-value pairs visible at level $i$.
nodes.title: Each skip-list level is a subsequence of the level below

nodes.summary: For a skip list and a level index $i$ (levels are numbered from $0$ at the bottom), level $i$ is the list of key-value pairs $(k, v)$ of the stored nodes whose tower height $h$ satisfies $i < h$, in the order in which these nodes appear in the bottom-level list of the skip list.
nodes.title: Level of a skip list

nodes.summary: For every skip list and every key $k$, the top-down skip-list lookup of $k$ returns the same result as looking up $k$ in the bottom-level abstraction, the list of key-value pairs of all stored nodes in order: the value of the first pair with key $k$, or no value if there is none.
nodes.title: Skip-list search agrees with bottom-level lookup

nodes.summary: If $S$ is a valid skip list and $k$, $k'$ are keys with $k' \ne k$, then looking up $k'$ in the skip list obtained by erasing $k$ from $S$ gives the same result as looking up $k'$ in $S$: the same value, or no value in both.
nodes.title: Erasure preserves lookups of other keys

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a valid skip list, that is, its keys are strictly increasing and every stored tower has positive height. For every key $k$, looking up $k$ in the skip list obtained from $L$ by erasing $k$ returns no value.
nodes.title: Erased keys are absent from a skip list

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every skip list $S$ with keys in $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$, all keys $k$ and $k'$ in $\alpha$ with $k' \ne k$, every value $v \in \beta$ and every requested height $h \in \mathbb{N}$, looking up $k'$ in the skip list obtained by inserting $k$ with value $v$ and requested height $h$ into $S$ gives the same result as looking up $k'$ in $S$.
nodes.title: Skip-list insertion does not change lookup of other keys

nodes.summary: For every skip list, key $k$, value $v$ and requested height $h$, looking up $k$ after inserting $k$ with value $v$ and requested height $h$ returns $v$.
nodes.title: Lookup after insertion returns the inserted value

nodes.summary: The lookup of a key $k$ in a skip list computes the search window for $k$, the suffix of the bottom-level nodes reached by descending from the highest level to level $0$, and returns the value of the first node in the window whose key is $k$, or no value if the window has no such node.
nodes.title: Skip-list lookup

nodes.summary: For every skip list and every key $k$, the search window for $k$ is a suffix of the list of the skip list's bottom-level nodes.
nodes.title: The search window is a suffix of the bottom level

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a key and let $H$ be the greatest tower height in a skip list ($H = 0$ if the list is empty or every tower has height $0$). Start with the full list of bottom-level nodes, and for each level $i$ from $H - 1$ down to $0$ in turn (no levels when $H = 0$) replace the current list by the result of advancing at level $i$: within the longest initial segment of the current list whose keys are all less than $k$,…
nodes.title: Skip-list search window

nodes.summary: A deterministic skip list with keys in $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$ is represented by the list of its bottom-level nodes, each node an entry carrying a key in $\alpha$, a value in $\beta$ and a tower height, a natural number. No ordering or height condition is imposed by this structure.
nodes.title: Skip list

nodes.summary: For every linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and every type $\beta$, the empty skip list with keys in $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$ is valid.
nodes.title: The empty skip list is valid

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a valid skip list, that is, its keys are strictly increasing and every stored tower has positive height. For every key $k$, the skip list obtained from $L$ by erasing $k$ is again valid.
nodes.title: Erasure preserves skip-list validity

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and $\beta$ a type. If a skip list with keys in $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$ is valid, then for every key $k \in \alpha$, value $v \in \beta$ and requested height $h \in \mathbb{N}$ (including $h = 0$), inserting $k$ with value $v$ and requested height $h$ yields a valid skip list. This covers both a new key and a key already present, whose value is replaced.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves skip-list validity

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. A skip list with keys in $\alpha$ and values in $\beta$ is valid when the keys of its bottom-level nodes are strictly increasing along the list and every node has a tower of positive height.
nodes.title: Valid skip list

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
